dedupe_keys.name: united states data center energy usage report lbnl 2024

description: The 2024 United States Data Center Energy Usage Report, led by Arman Shehabi at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory and required by the Energy Act of 2020 as an update to LBNL's 2016 study, estimates the electricity use of US data centres from 2014 to 2023 and gives a scenario range of future demand to 2028. It builds a bottom-up model from server, storage and network equipment shipment data and installed bases, with new treatment of accelerated servers for artificial intelligence, cooling system types and outdoor temperatures in modelling power usage effectiveness and water usage effectiveness, carbon and water footprints from local grid mixes, and an estimate for cryptocurrency mining. It finds that data centres used about 4.4 percent of US electricity in 2023 and could use between 6.7 and 12 percent by 2028. Coverage: the United States as a whole, annual values by data-centre type (hyperscale, colocation, enterprise and others) and equipment class. Format and access: a free PDF report with tables and figures from LBNL's publication sites and eScholarship; it is a US government-funded work that can be cited freely. Caveats: national totals only, no site-level data; results rest on shipment estimates and assumptions that the report documents; scenarios are not forecasts. Simulation uses: demand projections for power system capacity planning, environmental impact of data centres, and scenario inputs for electricity and water planning where data centres cluster. Related records: the IEA Energy and AI data give global estimates, the EU data centre reporting database gives European site-reported data, and CloudSim-type simulators model individual facilities.
